**Synopsis:**
Japanese importers and corporates are increasingly turning to FX hedging instruments — forwards, futures, options, and long-term supplier contracts — to protect against persistent yen weakness. The yen sits near 40-year lows (~159/USD), driven by Japan's low interest rate environment, slow BoJ hiking pace, and fiscal concerns under PM Takaichi. Market consensus is sceptical of any structural yen reversal, with the 155–165 range seen as the dominant regime. Hedging tenors have extended dramatically, from months to 5–10 years. Even exporters are beginning to hedge against a potential yen rebound to lock in overseas profits.

**Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?**
Sentiment: -10 — The article's forward-looking FX tone implies the market does not anticipate meaningful US rate cuts (which would close the US-Japan differential and support the yen). The scepticism expressed by JPMorgan and BofA desks that USD/JPY will stay in the 155–165 range reflects an implicit view that US rates remain elevated relative to Japan for the foreseeable future — slightly dovish bias acknowledged but insufficient to shift the structural dynamic.
